main_text.l: DE Naturæ variis motibus, ac muta-
mus. Missis igitur variis hujus vo-
attinet institutum, per Naturam intelligimus internum
illud principium, quo res quævis cum est, &
esse perfistit, tum agendi, patiendique, item ab
iisdem cessandi habet potentiam. Res autem quæ
intimum hoc principium causamque habent, naturales
vocantur, quo nomine maximè ab artificialibus
eas excludere intendimus. Neque enim obscurum
est res alias dici naturales, alias artificiales. Na-
turales, ut animantia cuncta, partesque illorum, stirpium
quoque, nec non concharum, unionumque genus universum: omnia demum quæ ex terræ viscē-

page.notes: The title block, LIBRI DUO and the division headings are set in mixed sizes and spaced capitals; the rendering above follows the printed words. Printed "RERVM", "NATVRALIVM", "DVO", "VNIVERSVM" and "PRIMVS" were given modern u/v spelling as the transcription rule requires. Page number and running head are not printed on this page. The woodcut initial D is joined to "Naturæ" as "DE". The word at the line end "viscē-" is a hyphenated break and the continuation is on the next page.
